questions.prompt: Two fingers with no friction pinch an object. What can the grasp resist?
options: Only torques, because the two normal forces are equal and opposite
Its weight, as long as the squeeze force is made large enough to hold it
Nothing vertical: without friction the contacts can only push along their normals
Any force at all, as long as the two normals are exactly opposite
questions.explanation: Frictionless contacts apply forces along the normals only, so a vertical load is not resisted.

questions.prompt: Parallel-jaw grasp, mass 1.2 kg, mu = 0.35, centred load, no acceleration, g = 9.81. Normal force per finger in N (two decimals)?
Same object (mu = 0.35, half-width a = 0.03 m) with the centre of mass 0.015 m off-centre. Normal force per finger in N (two decimals)?
Friction cone half-angle for mu = 0.5 in degrees (one decimal)?
Fingers at (-0.03, 0) and (0.03, 0.04) with horizontal inward normals and mu = 0.5. Is the grasp antipodal?

remediationRefs.label: Review: Antipodal grasp and force closure

options: No: the contact line is 33.7 degrees from the normals, outside the 26.6 degree friction cone
Yes: the normals are horizontal and opposite, so the grasp is antipodal for any friction
Cannot be decided without knowing the object's mass and the grip force
Yes: any two fingers pressing inward on the object form an antipodal grasp
questions.explanation: The contact line must lie inside both cones: 33.7 degrees > 26.6 degrees.

questions.prompt: What does force closure of a grasp mean?

remediationRefs.label: Review: Antipodal grasp and force closure

options: The object cannot be moved by the hand once the fingers are closed
The contact forces within the friction cones can balance any external wrench
The friction coefficient at every contact is at least one, so the cones are wide
The fingers have closed fully around the object and no gap remains
questions.explanation: The cone of contact wrenches spans the whole wrench space.

questions.prompt: You must verify that a planned two-finger grasp holds a 0.5 kg tool while the arm accelerates up to 8 m/s^2 in any direction. Outline the analysis and the physical check.
rubric: Computes the apparent weight envelope m(g +- a) and handles COM offset (torque) with the squeeze formula or grasp-map solver.
Checks antipodal alignment and uses a measured, conservative mu with a safety factor.
Describes a physical slip test that could reject the friction assumption.
